arxiv-2108-01869.title: Learning Task Agnostic Skills with Data-driven Guidance
arxiv-2108-01869.creator: Even Klemsdal, Sverre Herland, Abdulmajid Murad
arxiv-2108-01869.description: Abstract To increase autonomy in reinforcement learning, agents need to learn useful behaviours without reliance on manually designed reward functions. To that end, skill discovery methods have been used to learn the intrinsic options available to an agent using task-agnostic objectives.

arxiv-2210-11525.creator: Francis X. Diebold

Key words : Mitigation, Climate capture and storage, Sequestration Contact: fdiebold@sas.upenn.

arxiv-2402-16075.title: Don’t Start from Scratch: Behavioral Refinement via Interpolant-based Policy Diffusion
arxiv-2402-16075.creator: Kaiqi Chen, Eugene Lim, Kelvin Lin, Yiyang Chen, Harold Soh
arxiv-2402-16075.description: Abstract Imitation learning empowers artificial agents to mimic behavior by learning from demonstrations. Recently, diffusion models, which have the ability to model high-dimensional and multimodal distributions, have shown impressive performance on imitation learning tasks. These models learn to shape a policy by diffusing actions (or states) from standard Gaussian noise.

arxiv-2406-14015.title: CohortNet: Empowering Cohort Discovery for Interpretable Healthcare Analytics
arxiv-2406-14015.creator: Qingpeng Cai, Kaiping Zheng, H. V. Jagadish, Beng Chin Ooi, James Yip
arxiv-2406-14015.description: Abstract . Cohort studies are of significant importance in the field of healthcare analysis. However, existing methods typically involve manual, labor-intensive, and expert-driven pattern definitions or rely on simplistic clustering techniques that lack medical relevance. Automating cohort studies with interpretable patterns has great potential to facilitate healthcare analysis but remains an unmet need in prior research efforts.

pmc-10802106.title: Targeting autophagy in Alzheimer’s disease: Animal models and mechanisms
pmc-10802106.creator: Xiao-Wen Zhang, Xiang-Xing Zhu, Dong-Sheng Tang, Jia-Hong Lu
pmc-10802106.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an age-related progressive neurodegenerative disorder that leads to cognitive impairment and memory loss. Emerging evidence suggests that autophagy plays an important role in the pathogenesis of AD through the regulation of amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau metabolism, and that autophagy dysfunction exacerbates amyloidosis and tau pathology.

Smoking history was obtained.

pmc-11607133.title: Rare Case of Germline GATA2 ‐Deficiency With Merkel Cell Carcinoma and Acute Myeloid Leukemia
pmc-11607133.creator: SooHo Yu, Min‐Seung Park, Gyu Yeong Kim, Junhun Cho, Chul Won Jung, Hee‐Jin Kim, Hyun‐Young Kim
pmc-11607133.description: BackgroundGermline GATA2‐deficiency usually manifests as immunodeficiencies and myeloid neoplasms and sometimes with dermatological diseases, including warts, panniculitis, and skin cancers.CaseWe report a 36‐year‐old woman with germline GATA2‐deficiency who developed Merkel cell carcinoma followed by acute myeloid leukemia. Molecular analysis revealed a germline GATA2 S447R variant, not reported from the previous reported case, suggesting a potential association with Merkel cell carcinoma.

pmc-12619245.title: Time trends in cluster profiles of psychosomatic problems, self-rated poor health, and low life satisfaction from 2002 to 2022 among adolescents in five Nordic countries
pmc-12619245.creator: Einar Thorsteinsson, Håkan Stattin, Charli Eriksson
pmc-12619245.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe aim was to perform person-oriented analyses among adolescents in five Nordic countries to estimate changes from 2002 to 2022 based on three key indicators of poor health status: psychosomatic complaints, self-rated poor health, and poor life satisfaction.MethodsData were employed from the HBSC survey of 15-year-olds (2002 to 2022) from five Nordic countries (N = 48,320): Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. Cluster analyses were performed.ResultsSeven cluster profiles were identified. There were small differences between countries based on these profiles.

pmc-12766824.title: Machine learning prediction of germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants in patients with ovarian cancer
pmc-12766824.creator: Giovanni Innella, Giulia Erini, Antonio De Leo, Lea Godino, Luca Caramanna, Simona Ferrari, Sara Miccoli, Anna Myriam Perrone, Claudio Zamagni, Pierandrea De Iaco, Daniela Turchetti, Paola Rucci
pmc-12766824.description: ObjectivesTo assess the performance of machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict the presence of germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants in ovarian cancer (OC) patients based on clinical–pathological features.MethodsClinical–pathological features of 648 patients with OC tested for BRCA1/2 were analysed using three supervised ML algorithms: random forest, boosting and support vector machine.

pmc-12830530.title: Research Progress of Lipid Metabolism-Mediated Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-12830530.creator: Yuzhen Shen, Xiaoran Wang, Xinyu Liu, Guoying Wang, Xueqin Hou, Xiaoming Zhou
pmc-12830530.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease closely associated with age. The main clinical manifestations include cognitive impairment, including visuospatial ability, memory, language, and behavioral disorders. These manifestations considerably impair the patients’ ability to perform daily activities. Although the pathogenesis of AD remains unclear, many studies have confirmed the essential role of abnormal lipid metabolism and inflammatory response in AD occurrence and progression.

pmc-13068909.title: Exploring molecular mechanisms of aminoglycoside resistance in Escherichia coli MG1655 using the antibiotic resistance growth plate
pmc-13068909.creator: LBL Cullen, CJL Eldridge, BP Jones, G Forster-Wilkins, S P Lawton, MD Fielder
pmc-13068909.description: The overuse of antibiotics in human and animal health has driven the rapid emergence of multi-drug-resistant bacterial strains. To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance, we developed the Antibiotic Resistance Growth Plate (ARGP), an experimental evolution tool that imposes a spatiotemporal antibiotic gradient.

pmc-13211600.title: Machine Learning–Based Survival Prediction Models for Young Patients With Gastric Cancer: Model Development and Validation Study
pmc-13211600.creator: Ha Ye Jin Kang, Wooyeong Jang, Minsam Ko, Kwang Sun Ryu, Matthew Balcarras
pmc-13211600.description: BackgroundDespite a global decline in the incidence of gastric cancer (GC), the number of cases diagnosed among younger individuals continues to increase. Several studies have been conducted to develop predictive models of mortality in patients with GC.ObjectiveWe developed 3- and 5-year survival prediction models for young patients with GC based on machine learning–based survival modeling approaches.

pmc-13225540.title: Reevaluating the nature of thymic lipofibroadenoma: A case report with hamartomatous features and a literature review
pmc-13225540.creator: Ning Zhou, Shuya Hu, Liqiao Chen, Hegang Wu, Fanrong Wang
pmc-13225540.description: Rationale:Thymic lipofibroadenoma (LFA) is an extremely rare benign thymic tumor of mixed epithelial and mesenchymal origin, whose pathological nature remains incompletely understood. This case presents a unique thymic lesion combining classic LFA features with a novel lobulated, ductal-forming epithelial proliferation, prompting a reevaluation of its classification.

pmc-13342647.title: Robust unsupervised outlier detection in IoT using contrastive learning-driven autoencoders
pmc-13342647.creator: Shengyu Gu
pmc-13342647.description: Outlier detection plays a critical role in ensuring the reliability, security, and operational stability of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, where data streams are often high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and unlabeled. In this paper, we propose a robust unsupervised outlier detection framework that integrates autoencoder-based representation learning with contrastive loss to enhance discriminative capability in latent space.
